newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 0.9 pct w/e May 10 - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 0.9 pct w/e May 10 - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.9 percent in the period ending May 10 versus April's revised final estimate, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 6.4 percent compared to the same period a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 6.4 percent in the week ended May 10 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
The report said overall, retailers contacted were slightly more optimistic than before about business fundamentals.
Discount stores reported an uptick in sales of seasonal goods, and apparel continued to sell well, especially higher-priced lines carried by regional department stores.
Meanwhile, department stores said sales of home furnishings and hard lines were slow.
Howard Eilenberg, retail analyst at Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc, said he was optimistic about sales in the coming weeks.
"The next couple of weeks should look pretty good. They should pick-up," Eilenberg said in an interview on Reuters Financial Television.
Eisenberg forecast a slower growth rate in retail sales and the economy for the second quarter.
"I don't think the first quarter's pace could be continued," he said.
